message: Thank you for reaching out, Elena Rowan. Let me start with a quick diagnostic.

Oversized images are the main issue identified by the initial report that just arrived.

Pending my backend review, my current checklist is:
1) Start by fixing the bloated images (the primary concern right now)
2) Afterward, clean up the other key Pagespeed-related issues
3) Review the backend cache configuration
With access to the site, I should be able to sort this out pretty quickly.
Could you give me your estimate in hours?

The image issue should take just 45 minutes. After that, I would spend the next 4 hours reviewing the rest of the setup to ensure there are no other lingering issues.

Since I'm trying to build my Upwork profile at this point, I'm happy to get it sorted for a cup of coffee.
Although the site has accumulated many legacy pages over time, we're currently testing the link I sent as our new webpage. So yes, please proceed.
We ran the earlier test against https://harborlineadvisors.example.
Yes, this is the correct site.

Is HLX the new upcoming theme being tested?
https://harborlineadvisors.example/hlx
Yes.
The problem with that one is definitely in the cache configuration.
Before you share access to the backend and hosting, is there anything you'd like me to clarify?
No, if $85 works for you, I'll send you an initial project and can also grant hosting and Wordpress access.
That works for me, sure.

Before I can proceed, could you provide the following? Thank you for the offer.

\- WP Engine hosting access
\- WordPress admin access, including plugin/cache permissions
\- Is there any third-party CDN in use, such as CloudFlare?
There isn't any third-party CDN.
https://harborlineadvisors.example/wp-admin/?wtlwp_token=FAKE_TOKEN_0000000000000000

And to clarify
1) Do you need me to address the pagespeed issue for https://harborlineadvisors.example/hlx specifically? or the original https://harborlineadvisors.example as well?
Please review both; HLX is the new test.
Sure
Which email address should I use for the WP Engine invitation?
The email address you can use is clients@brightpixel-digital.example.
Ok sent
Invitation received, many thanks.
Because our access doesn't permit any page editing, this might block the remediation work.
I'll look into it.
While the access issue is being investigated, I'll review the Cache configuration issue.

After discovering that WP engine had tried to troubleshoot this today without my knowing, I'm chatting with them now. Their work appears to have changed the entire site; we lost many fonts and much of the formatting, particularly on the Legacy site.
Until the current incident is resolved, I'll leave the site unchanged and won't make any changes.

1) Was it only recently that the page speed issue started?

2) Can you remember whether any recent changes might have affected it?
Before this incident, the legacy pages had been working without problems. I just built out HLX this week.
The site is back to its earlier state now; WP Engine completed the revert.
I hadn't realized the Thrive license had expired, so I'll need to look into it.
A possible cause is the expiration: multiple Thrive plugins call home when their license expires. Could you check the license expiration date and compare it with when the issue began?
Is Thrive active again now? That's how it appears.
When the site is viewed through an admin account, one thing stands out: it runs really fast.
Previously, I brought in an optimization expert to work on the site.
At the moment, Thrive does appear to be functional. Was the earlier problem caused by the license?
Were these other pages also created by you, by any chance? They look malicious and are tied to a user named **cobalt_orchard_13**.
The one I created was HLX; I didn't make any of the others.
This user appears to be responsible for creating 823 pages.
Most of this casino-related content was published in December.
Since this pattern typically points to a WordPress site compromised with malware, please confirm whether these pages are legitimate.
I didn't create that.
The cause isn't clear to me, though the activity appears recent.
Given that, we'll make site security remediation our first priority immediately.
Of the users shown here, could you identify any accounts that don't belong to the site?
Illegal casino ads are probably being run through your domain by hackers.
Can you explain what might have caused that to happen?
Has anyone else been given access recently?
We haven't granted anyone else access, but we can remove everyone.
Although this user has existed since 2022, it only began posting recently, on December 3rd.
The slow-page issue may be connected to this, I think.
Yes, that explanation seems reasonable.
Unfortunately, our former administrator Marcus Bennett may have been involved.

These three accounts belong to me:
elena@harborlineadvisors.example
elena@stonefieldroyalties.example
elena.rowan@mail.example

Everyone else can be removed.
Before we return to reviewing the page-speed issue, I'll prioritize securing the site. Understood.
Please confirm whether I may proceed with the following work; it falls outside the original job scope.

Under the proposed cleanup, every post by cobalt_orchard_13 would be deleted, and any user absent from the list above would be removed. The site would also receive Wordfence, installed as a security scanner to review its plugins and themes for exploits that may have been inserted.
Yes.
Our most recent Thrive Architect installation might be connected to this.
Understood, I'll move forward.
Removing the admins may be blocked because my temporary access doesn't seem to include the necessary permission.
Should I use the same email when I grant you the additional access?
Alternatively, I can delete the administrator accounts myself—one second.
I sent the invite to the same email.
Use clients@brightpixel-digital.example for the invitation.
I still haven't received the invitation email.
Resent
The resent invitation arrived, thanks.
My account is currently a Subscriber; to enable the required work, you'll need to change its type to Admin.
Your account appears to have been deleted; that's strange.
Access is working now; I'm in.
Ok
Since this is a business page, the comment feature probably isn't needed. Do you use it at all? If not, I'd disable it too.
That feature isn't something we use.

Current update: Security scans are running now. So far, I have manually removed 823 posts and 9 pages. I have also removed permissions from 6 offending users, but I'll retain those accounts until I've identified all malicious content. Additional areas of the site are now being tightened.
Ok

The checks found no impact to the following:
- Media
- Comments
- Widgets
- The theme's functions.php file

Wordfence is now configured as an antivirus-style security scanner; it will run automatically and block potential attacks.

XML-RPC is currently disabled. If you use a third-party app or site to manage WordPress, let me know, because it must be enabled.
Ok.
As for the original site-speed issue, what, if anything, do you think could be behind it?
Unfortunately, I have bad news: the site is indeed infected with malware. Several injected "fake" plugins created all these unauthorized administrator users.
A few have been identified so far.
Backdoor access is provided by the identified malicious artifacts.
I'm going to need a day to clean them up. Once that's complete, I'll monitor the system to see whether they reinfect it.
Unless these files are completely removed, they can replicate and recreate the administrator users.
I'll continue posting updates here as remediation progresses. Because there is no quick workaround for this, unfortunately, it won't be finished within an hour or two.
Ok
On WP-Engine, I manually triggered a backup; it should notify you by email later.
If you're interested, I can share a few examples.
Thanks for sending these; they look good.

There are probably two quick options for this issue:

1) Because WP Engine has backend server tools that are more effective for security scanning and removal, one route is to ask its support team for Malware Remediation. A definite contributor is wp-content/mu-plugins/cache-sync-guard.php.

2) Another route is to restore an earlier version of your site's backup. Have you made any changes to the site recently? If so, do you remember when any plugins or pages were added? The issue seems to coincide with additions involving Thrive Leads, Contact Form 7, GTM, and Simple Google Recaptcha around 12th-16th December.
I'll contact WP Engine about option #1. Earlier backup versions are available, but I'm unsure when the malware began; that administrator user appears to have been there for quite a while.
That does seem likely; it could have been dormant. Malware can infect a site earlier and remain inactive for weeks or months before activating.
Reference link: https://harborlineadvisors.example/
For the moment, it seems to be working.
I'm in touch with wpengine now.
After disabling 11 infected plugins and removing 6 replicator files, the site's speed appears to have returned to normal.
Could you try the site now?
Yes, the site looks satisfactory.
So the evidence confirms that the site issue was caused by malware after all 😅

Over the next 24 hours, I’ll run another round of security scans and monitor for any recurrence. Thank you for staying responsive throughout this security review; with any luck, the problem is now resolved.
Approved, please proceed with scans and monitoring.
Good night, Elena Rowan—and you’re welcome!

Hi Elena Rowan, after a day of digging, here is the complete rundown.

The problem went beyond the fake administrator users we found last night. A hidden administrator account was also buried in the database, and around 830 casino spam pages had been published under that account. Code injected into one of your plugins concealed all of this while interfering with the site’s caching, which caused visitor pages to take 15+ seconds to load.

The identified malware and content have now been cleaned up, taking about 7 hours in total today. The work included:
- Removing the hidden administrator account and all ~830 spam pages
- Replacing the compromised plugin with a clean official copy
- Reinstalling WordPress itself
- Working with WP Engine to reset the site’s credentials and keys, while also requesting a full platform-level malware scan for independent confirmation
- Configuring Wordfence to scan for security issues and alert us if suspicious activity returns

Pages now load in under 2 seconds instead of 16. I’ll continue monitoring the site for the next couple of days to verify that it remains clean.

I need you to complete a few steps:
1\. Because the security reset signed everyone out of WordPress, set a new password when you log back in and ask every other administrator to do likewise.
2\. As an additional precaution, change your WP Engine password.
3\. Give me full access to your Google Search Console so I can remove the spam pages from Google before they damage your rankings. Go to Settings > Users and permissions > Add user > Full access and use theo@brightpixel-digital.example.
4\. Submit a quick test through the contact form and confirm that its email arrives, ensuring your leads still flow after these changes.

The remaining work is:
- Cleaning up Search Console once access is available
- Updating the outdated plugins, which were probably the attackers’ original entry point
- Sharing the results from WP Engine when its scan is returned

I’m happy to answer questions. If you would like a formal written report for your records, I can provide one as well.
The invite for Google search console has been sent. Thanks for the update.

I’ve now submitted removal requests for 46 of the offending links, Elena Rowan, to prevent deterioration of the website’s search trust rating. They are awaiting approval, and I’ll update you once that happens.

There are a few more urgent matters to address:

1) I traced the issue back to Thrive Apprentice. The hackers exploited it to insert the malware, so it should be updated; however, WordPress does not appear to provide an update option here. Can you give me access to the theme provider’s portal so I can find the required files?

2) I believe you received an email about downloading a site backup, apparently from 2026. Please share its download link so I can manually compare that backup with the current site and weed out any remaining hidden malware.

3) Please remember to update the passwords for WP Engine and WP Admin, including every individual account, and test the Contact Form to verify that messages still reach your mailbox.
A previous developer installed Thrive, but it might not be licensed. If that is the case, perhaps we’ll need to remove it.
I've updated every relevant password.
According to the email from wpengine, the file is in the “backups” area. If you want, I can download and deliver it; the email included this link.
<https://hosting-portal.example/email-link/e0033>
Since it appears to be configured as the theme, are any of its utilities used when you create pages or for similar work?
Using this backup file, I’ll try to carry out a secondary review. Thanks, Elena Rowan.
For page creation, I do use thrive on the current site. However, we built the new site without Thrive, and I can move the landing pages and new pages over to elmentor.

Removing the page builder now would break the current site because it does more than build pages; its features often control how those pages are styled and displayed. Full removal may therefore have to wait until the new site is ready.

As an interim step, I’ll disable Thrive Apprentice, which is the plugin providing the learning-platform functionality.
Because this opens the WP Engine backup page, I don’t believe it is the correct link. The required link should download a ZIP file directly, and I think WP Engine emailed it to you a day ago.
<https://files.harborlineadvisors.example/folders/e0035>
I uploaded the last three downloads to google drive. There is also a screenshot showing the IDs, which should help you determine which file is which.

**For the malware**
The files are now appearing on my side as well, thank you. I’m still attempting to download the Nov 12th preinfection version identified by checkpoint 2649137084, and I’ve just made another request.

**For speed optimization**
The necessary optimizations are now configured. Desktop performance has made good progress and is averaging 74 on average, while the mobile score remains at 41; I’ve attached the Before and After results. The remaining mobile penalties are:
- A queue containing too many fonts: 9 different fonts are loaded for the site, which is a design issue
- Stape Conversion Tracking has its "Container URL" pointed at what appears to be an unrelated site. Was that intentional? http://load.dev.harborlineadvisors.example

The desktop analysis is available here: https://pagespeed-report.example/analysis/https-harborlineadvisors-example/f66k-sample?form_factor=desktop

For both mobile and desktop, the site now loads at a good speed according to largest content paint. It is already functioning as it should, although several remaining items are lowering the scores.

If you want to pursue a higher score, we can continue working together by discussing the removal of unused plugins, fonts that can be converted, and—most importantly—the GTM and pixel configuration currently spread across multiple plugins.

Thanks, Elena Rowan. Let me know what you think.
I’m happy with how it looks, so let’s wrap up the work for now.
That works for me; we can wrap up. If any of the adjustments have left something out of place or caused a feature to stop working correctly, please let me know.
I really appreciate all your help in making the troubleshooting process go so smoothly. Thank you.
What was the total number of hours you spent?

Apologies for getting back to you late. Once you are satisfied, please remove my access from WordPress, WP Engine, and Search Console.

Here is the current status:
1) **Search results:** The cleanup has been completed and approved.
2) **WP Engine Support:** They responded and confirmed that all remaining traces were removed, so we can be confident the issue is behind us.
3) **Plugins:** Everything is now up to date, and plugins judged to be high risk were either removed or disabled.
4) **Post Tags:** I also located and cleared additional post tags left over from the earlier spam.
5) **Autoptimize plugin:** For future reference, this was installed to handle page-speed adjustments.

The first day took about 7 hours, followed by another 3 hours to finish the remaining cleanup and page-optimization work.

The bonus notification just came through, Elena Rowan—thank you, I truly appreciate it!

Provided everything is in order, I’ll conclude the contract. With WordFence configured for automated protection, the site should generally be much more secure.

If anything goes wrong later or you need help in another area, feel free to contact me at any time. If you’re satisfied with the work, please consider leaving feedback for the project. Thanks again!
It looks as though the theme may have taken our pages down. Can you repair this site’s theme?
Affected site: https://stonefieldroyalties.example
I’ll take a look at the problem, Elena Rowan. Certainly.
To investigate this, could you provide access to both the site and WP-Engine?
My understanding is that you should still have access to wpengine.
I’ve sent the password-reset message for site administrator access.
Access reset received, much appreciated.

Before I can proceed, could you provide more detail about the issue?

1) Was anyone working on the site immediately before the error occurred?
2) How many pages does the error affect?
Investigating
Malware may have affected this site as well. I’ll investigate further to confirm.
The message referenced above came from WP Engine. I cannot see any users there, and we did not use Thrive on this site.
The infinite theme definitely contains malware.
That was the early warning sign. We should also configure wordfence so the site is secured.
Okay—that is surprising, since if I remember correctly, this site doesn’t have thrive.

At this stage, the attacks do not necessarily target only one exploit. They automatically generate various kinds of spam, check for broken plugins or themes you own, and then use any they find as a backdoor.
On Harborline, for instance, Wordfence is actively blocking these attacks.
Ok

Hidden users are definitely present, and the situation closely resembles the incident on Harborline.

The database contains 14 accounts, whereas only 13 visible accounts appear in Wp-admin.
While we have the opportunity, could you also review the administrator list and tell me which accounts should be removed?
Now that the scan results have returned, I’m confident malware has taken over the site. Please let me know whether you would like me to proceed with remediation.
Yes

Okay, I will start diving in.

1) Could you trigger the Download Backup option for both the newest and oldest backup? (2644011208) Oct 20th and (2647181629) December 18th. With any luck if that version is clean, it will speed up a lot of the work.
https://hosting-portal.example/installs/stonefieldroy/backup_points

2) Any idea when did the site stopped working?
I don't use this site much, so I'm not sure when it stopped working.
A similar theme problem came up before and was easy to fix, though I'm unsure whether the same solution applies here.
Okay, requested backup download triggered manually.
To prevent any further access, I'll remove the selected user accounts; please let me know which users you want removed.
I was just about to head off for the day—impeccable timing :D
Except for elena@stonefieldroyalties.example, every user account can be removed.
Got it
All your pages and posts were moved to the trash on this website, causing them to appear blank. Yup, it’s the same casino malware.
Shoot ok

Because the earliest version appears too dated, I need another favor from you with the backup:
https://hosting-portal.example/installs/stonefieldroy/backup_points

2648615302 - December 4th
2645879433 - November 11th
done

The backup checkpoints show that the infection spread incrementally over time across various areas of the website. Some recorded dates go as far back as September. Pretty interesting engineering, to be honest.

I’m going to make another fresh attempt, as this was an extremely challenging case.

\- I detected and removed 37 distinct malicious backdoors. That number suggests the site was probably hacked by several parties.
\- The earliest attack files were uploaded in September, while all the malware spam posts arrived in October.
\- Given the severity, restoring a backup from an earlier point is the best approach. However, the earliest version available on WP-Engine was made on October 20th, and it is infected as well.
\- The removal is complete, but some issues remain with the page and post status.

\-----

Because I have not previously seen any of these pages, I cannot visually verify whether they are the correct originals. Please review the Pages link below and identify whether the recovered pages are the original ones:
<https://stonefieldroyalties.example/wp-admin/edit.php?post_type=page>
Sounds good.

Sorry I missed my earlier follow-up.

**Latest update.**
According to the database, every page was moved to Trash on December 20th, causing the website to stop functioning completely.

The website now appears normal again after we restored 10th November's backup. We are using this restored version as the baseline for the malware-removal work.

Current status: the site layout has been fully recovered, Wordfence has been configured for security, malware has been removed from around 34 outdated plugins, and all fake admins have been removed.

Follow-up work remains. Although the pages appear fine, I cannot verify whether all the private pages work correctly. Please test every contact form and change your admin password. For the search-engine cleanup, I still need Search Console access for Stonefield as well.

**Overall report**
There are signs of earlier, smaller-scale attacks dating back to 2022. The majority of the 14000 posts were injected on October 14th, and all of the website's pages were deleted on December 20th.
Looks good.
You should still have access, since Stonefield uses the same search console as Harborline.
Full account access was not provided, I think; it appears the sharing was handled separately for each Property (website).
Please see if access works now.
Yes, the requested access now works.
The submission is now complete, with about 130 links sent. Compared with last time, this set is much heavier and contains a mix of pornography and casino links.
We can probably conclude the remediation for this site as well, since WP Engine's internal scan has also given it a clean bill of health.
Feel free to contact me if anything looks out of place or if I have missed something!
Great
What was the total number of hours you spent?
The total comes to about 16.5 hours.
So that you can receive more work history and feedback, I issued a separate $425 contract for the Stonefield work.
Thanks for arranging that, Elena Rowan—it’s perfect! 🙌

Hi Elena Rowan, I appreciate the additional payment for the extra work, and thanks again for making this such an easy one. I’m happy to help if anything comes up with the site later. Have a great weekend ahead. Cheers, Theo Vale!
